```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggplot2)

key <- isTRUE(params$key)

# ---- Plot style (matches the other handouts) ----
theme_set(
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_line(linewidth = 0.2),
      plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 2, 4)
    )
)

# ---- Data ----
# After class, save the Google Form responses as data/field-goals.csv with
# columns dist_cm (number) and success (0 or 1), then re-render the key. Until
# then, the key uses simulated data.
fg_file <- "../data/field-goals.csv"
simulated <- !file.exists(fg_file)
if (simulated) {
  set.seed(722)
  n <- 36
  dist_cm <- sample(10:50, n, replace = TRUE)
  field_goals <- data.frame(
    dist_cm = dist_cm,
    success = rbinom(n, 1, plogis(3.2 - 0.1 * dist_cm))
  )
} else {
  field_goals <- read.csv(fg_file)
}

fg_glm <- glm(
  success ~ dist_cm,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  data = field_goals
)
b0 <- coef(fg_glm)[["(Intercept)"]]
b1 <- coef(fg_glm)[["dist_cm"]]

dists <- seq(10, 50, by = 10)
logits <- b0 + b1 * dists
ps <- plogis(logits)
curve_grid <- data.frame(dist_cm = seq(10, 50, length.out = 101))
curve_grid$logit <- b0 + b1 * curve_grid$dist_cm
curve_grid$p <- plogis(curve_grid$logit)
table_points <- data.frame(dist_cm = dists, logit = logits, p = ps)

# ---- Helpers ----
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)

# A blank to fill in, or the answer in the key
fill <- function(x, width = "1.6cm") {
  if (key) as.character(x) else paste0("\\mbox{\\rule{", width, "}{0.4pt}}")
}

blank_lines <- function(n) {
  if (!key) cat(rep("\\vspace{0.3in}\n\n", n), sep = "")
}
answer <- function(...) if (key) cat(..., sep = "")

# Centered LaTeX table. header and each row are character vectors of cells.
latex_table <- function(header, rows, align) {
  row_tex <- vapply(rows, \(r) paste(r, collapse = " & "), character(1))
  cat(
    "\\begin{center}",
    "\\renewcommand{\\arraystretch}{1.8}",
    paste0("\\begin{tabular}{", align, "}"),
    "\\toprule",
    paste(paste(header, collapse = " & "), "\\\\"),
    "\\midrule",
    paste(row_tex, "\\\\"),
    "\\bottomrule",
    "\\end{tabular}",
    "\\end{center}",
    sep = "\n"
  )
  cat("\n\n")
}

# Empty axes spanning the distances in the activity, with a grid to draw on
dist_axes <- function(ylab, ylim, ybreaks, ylabels = ybreaks) {
  ggplot(data.frame(dist_cm = c(10, 50), y = ylim), aes(dist_cm, y)) +
    geom_blank() +
    scale_x_continuous(
      "Distance (cm)",
      limits = c(8, 52),
      breaks = dists,
      minor_breaks = seq(10, 50, by = 5)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(ylab, limits = ylim, breaks = ybreaks, labels = ylabels)
}

# Raw data: jittered 0s and 1s
data_layer <- function(alpha = 1) {
  geom_point(
    aes(dist_cm, success),
    data = field_goals,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 21,
    size = 2,
    alpha = alpha,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.04, seed = 1)
  )
}

# The five distances from the table, as open circles
table_layer <- function(y) {
  geom_point(
    aes(dist_cm, .data[[y]]),
    data = table_points,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    shape = 21,
    fill = "white",
    size = 2.5,
    stroke = 1
  )
}

# Range for the log odds axis: the key fits the fitted line, students label it
logit_lim <- range(c(-1, 1, pretty(logits)))
```

\doctitle{Field goals and logistic regression`r if (key) " (answer key)" else ""`}

Does the chance of kicking a paper field goal depend on distance? Each of you kicked once from a random distance between 10 and 50 cm and recorded whether you made it. Now we'll model the class's data.

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (key && simulated) {
  cat(
    "\\textit{Placeholder: this key uses simulated data. Save the class's",
    "responses as data/field-goals.csv and re-render.}\n\n"
  )
}
```

\vspace{2pt}\hrule\vspace{6pt}

$$
\text{logit}(p) = \log\left(\frac{p}{1 - p}\right)
\qquad\qquad
p = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\text{logit}(p)}}
$$

- $p$: probability of success, between 0 and 1
- $\text{logit}(p)$: the log odds of success, any value from $-\infty$ to $\infty$
- Left: from probability to log odds. Right: from log odds back to probability.

\vspace{2pt}\hrule

# 1. Draw the data

Sketch the class's data. Each kick is one point: its distance on the x-axis, and 0 (missed) or 1 (made it) on the y-axis.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 2.4
#| out-width: "70%"
p <- dist_axes("Success", c(-0.1, 1.1), c(0, 1))
if (key) {
  p <- p + data_layer()
}
p
```

# 2. Write the model

Write the model in statistical notation. What's the distribution of the response? What links $p$ to the linear equation?

```{r}
#| results: asis
blank_lines(3)
answer(
  "$$\n\\begin{aligned}\n",
  "\\text{success} &\\sim \\text{Bernoulli}(p) \\\\\n",
  "\\text{logit}(p) &= \\beta_0 + \\beta_1 \\text{dist\\_cm}\n",
  "\\end{aligned}\n$$\n\n"
)
```

# 3. Write down the coefficients

We'll fit the model in R.

```{=latex}
\begingroup\footnotesize
```

```r
fg_glm <- glm(success ~ dist_cm, family = binomial(link = "logit"), data = field_goals)
coef(fg_glm)
```

```{=latex}
\endgroup
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
latex_table(
  c("Term", "Coefficient", "Estimate"),
  list(
    c("\\texttt{(Intercept)}", "$\\beta_0$", fill(fmt(b0, 3))),
    c("\\texttt{dist\\_cm}", "$\\beta_1$", fill(fmt(b1, 3)))
  ),
  "llc"
)
```

\newpage

# 4. Draw the linear part

Draw $\text{logit}(p) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{dist\_cm}$. It's a straight line, so you only need two points. Label the y-axis first.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 2.6
#| out-width: "70%"
if (key) {
  dist_axes("logit(p)", logit_lim, pretty(logit_lim)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
    geom_line(aes(dist_cm, logit), data = curve_grid, linewidth = 1) +
    table_layer("logit")
} else {
  # Blank tick labels with room to the left to write them in
  dist_axes("logit(p)", c(-3, 3), -3:3, rep("", 7)) +
    theme(
      axis.ticks.length.y = unit(4, "pt"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 28))
    )
}
```

# 5. Calculate $p$

For each distance, calculate the log odds from your coefficients. Then convert the log odds to a probability.

```{r}
#| results: asis
rows <- lapply(seq_along(dists), \(i) {
  c(dists[i], fill(fmt(logits[i]), "2.2cm"), fill(fmt(ps[i]), "2.2cm"))
})
latex_table(
  c(
    "Distance (cm)",
    "$\\text{logit}(p) = \\beta_0 + \\beta_1 \\times \\text{distance}$",
    "$p = \\frac{1}{1 + e^{-\\text{logit}(p)}}$"
  ),
  rows,
  "ccc"
)
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
cat(
  "How much does $\\text{logit}(p)$ change between each row? ",
  fill(fmt(10 * b1), "2.2cm"),
  "\n\nHow much does $p$ change between each row? ",
  if (key) {
    paste(fmt(diff(ps)), collapse = ", ")
  } else {
    "\\mbox{\\rule{5cm}{0.4pt}}"
  },
  "\n\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

# 6. Draw the probabilities

Plot your five values of $p$, then connect them with a smooth curve. Add the data from Part 1.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 2.6
#| out-width: "70%"
p <- dist_axes("p (probability of success)", c(-0.1, 1.1), seq(0, 1, 0.25))
if (key) {
  p <- p +
    data_layer(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_line(aes(dist_cm, p), data = curve_grid, linewidth = 1) +
    table_layer("p")
}
p
```
